cells.location: CALICUT
cells.place: Single Copper-plate received from Shri K.V. John, Lecturer in Archaeology, Department of History, University of Calicut. Findspot: Mitrānḍapuram, Trivandrum, Trivandrum Taluk, Trivandrum District.
cells.remarks: Records the creation of an endowment of 600 paṛai of paddy and 30 Ānaichachu yielding an interest of 132 paṛai of paddy by Suvākaraṇ Maṇiyan of Malaiyamam to provide for food offerings to the deity Śrī Kṛishṇa Tiruvadi (Śrī Kiruṇḍan-tiruvadi) and to the Talakkirāma-dēvagal (Śāligrāmams), which he had set up in the maṇḍapa in the temple at Mitrānḍapuram. It mentions that 2 nāḷi of the above food-offerings should be given to the bhaṭṭar. Further, it records the provision of 12 paṛai of paddy for feeding the nambi who performs the śānti, to meet the expenses of a cooking vessel (uruḷi), a bell, a creeper-shaped lamp-stand and three bell-metal dishes. The donor is stated to have deposited three achchu into the treasury for the feeding of a brāhmaṇa on the day of dvādaśī. The names of the signatories including that of the donor and Kēśavan Tāmōdaran (Dāmōdaran) of Taraṇinallūr are mentioned at the end. In characters of about the 12th century. Published in T.A.S. Vol. III, pp. 21 ff and plate.

cells.location: KERALA / MALAPPURAM DISTRICT / MALAPPURAM TALUK / CALICUT — Kerala
cells.place: Set of five copper-plates. Do.
cells.remarks: States that the following grants of lands to provide for daily expenditure of the deity Paṭṭārakar (bhaṭṭāraka) of Mittirāṇḍapuram were entered under the orders of Kṛṣṇajña-paḷḷārar: 1) Lands in Veṇbāykkunṟam, Maṇṇarai, Iṇḍaṇūr, Meliṇḍaṇūr, Kōlach-chai-mūlai, etc. contributing the quantity of 117 paṟai, six naḻi by the measure Iḍaṅgaḻi and 3 uḻakku of paddy by Kuṅgaḻ-Kēraḷan under the orders of Kṛṣṇajña-paḷḷārar with the stipulation that the produce as specified may be collected on the day of Chittirai-vishū with effect from the month of Mithuna, when Jupiter was in Tulā; 2) Lands in various places including Tēvarpuḷimā, Kaṇichchikōḍu, Nechchikōḍu etc., by Seṉṉaṅgaṇḍan of Dēvarpaḷḷi towards the daily food offerings with five naḻi of rice offered half on each of the two occasions. Provision is also made for the perpetual lamps and to meet the expenses of śāntivrutti and the worship (sahasran.) In addition to these, lands and gardens (puraiyiḍam) from Vaḍuga-Brah-maśśēri, Paṇāhaṭṭūr, Agattikōḍu etc., were assigned to provide for food-offerings. A post script in different and later characters states that śrī-Māttaṇḍavarman of Kiḷ-appērūr ruling over Veṇāḍu is said to have granted the rājabhōga and taxes collected at Tiruvāṇ(n*)dapuram for the daily food-offerings and perpetual lamp to the deity. Ends with probably the sign-manual Iravi-pērūr. In characters of about the 13th century. ibid., pp. 1 ff. and plate.

cells.language: Sanskrit, Western variety of Southern alphabet.
cells.remarks: Issued from Aniruddhapura. Records the royal grant of the village Mandikalani situated in Taḷikāṭahāra-vishaya to the brāhmaṇa Śivasvāmin belonging to Kauṇḍinya-gōtra and Taittirīya-śākhā for the performance of bali, charu, vaiśvadeva and agnihōtra rites, for his own merit as well as that of his parents. It is also stated that one-sixth of the village granted was made over to Māṭṛisvāmin, the brother's son (bhrātṛivya), probably of the donee. The dūtaka was Śārdūla. The charter was engraved by Mahābalādhikṛita Mahāsāndhivigrahika Karkka. Published in Bhāratīya Itihāsa Aṇi Saṃskṛiti, January 1972, pp. 5 ff.

cells.location: MADRAS
cells.place: Impressions from the Director of Archaeology, Government of Tamil Nadu, Madras, through Shri P.R. Srinivasan. Findspot: Vēlañjēri, Tiruttani Taluk, Chingleput District, Tamil Nadu.
cells.remarks: The king is described as the first son of Kamapavarma and his queen Vijaya of the Ganga family. Kampavarma is said to have wrested the kingdom after defeating Nṛipatunga in battle. Records the royal grant of tax-free dēvadāna-brahmadēya by clubbing Pūdur with Mēliṛuñjēṛu as kāni to the sabhaiyār of the latter place stipulating that they should measure out 1000 kāḍi of paddy annually as pañchavāra to the deity Subrahmanya on the hill at Tiruttani, at the instance of the executor Brahmādhirāja is stated to be the executor (āṇatti). Poḍiṇi Mahādēva-bhaṭṭar composed the praśasti and Vijayannaṇ wrote the same.

cells.location: CHIṬYĀLĀPĀḌU
cells.place: Pillar lying in a field.
cells.date: Śaka 1135 (śara-loka-indu-bhū), Śrimukha, Madhu (Chaitra) śu. 8, Sunday, Pushya= 1213 A. D., March 31.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that Kāṭaya-śēnāni, son of Kāma-chamūpati and grandson of Kāṭaya-chamūpati constructed the temple along with prākāra, consecrated the image of Rudrēśvara and made some gift for the services, the details of which are lost. Kāṭaya (II) who is described as pratigaṇḍa-bhairava is stated to have received a simhāsana, the title of maṇḍalika and two chāmaras from his overlord who was pleased with his valour. Published in the Inss. of A.P., Warangal Dt., No. 52.

cells.location: KARNATAKA †
cells.place: Stone lying near residence of Fakhruddin.
cells.remarks: States that the chief of the Sinda family (name lost) was adminitering Ballakuṇḍa-vishaya and that on the orders of the king constructed a tirtha in stone and granted two [khā]r of land in a village (name not clear) for the same. Mentions Kundabbe as the queen of a Sinda chief (name lost) and states that she was associated in making some grant. The gift was probably entrusted to Viranandi munindra, on of the disciples of Kuṇḍakundānvaya and Dēśi-gaṇa, a disciple of Tīrthācharyya belonging to Nandi-saṁgha. The record is stated to have been written by Chhaṭṭayya, son of Puṭēyamayya. In characters of about the 11th century.

cells.remarks: Records a grant of the village Guṇḍigaṇūru in the province of Kuru-gōḍu and to the account of the treasury (in the charge) of Harivā-ṇada-rāja by Pratāpa Dēvarāya to Lakshmī-kānta-dīkshita as ēkabhōga-agrahāra for the purpose of the amṛipaḍi service of the deity Virūpāksha. Further states that on the family of Lakshmīkānta-dīkshita the grant village had reverted back to the government treasury and that (after some time), at the request of Rāmarājayya, on behalf of the sthānīkas, Sadāśivarāya-mahārāya granted half of the village for the same purpose, for which the original grant was made earlier, on the occasion of Ka[p]ila-shashṭhi for the merit of his father, Achyutarāya. The closing portion contains grants of wet-lands and a garden.

cells.date: Śaka 1388, Vyaya, Māgha śu. 10, Thursday, Rōhiṇi, Brahmayōga, ....Jākaraṇa, Kumbhalagna = 1467 A.D., January 15.
cells.remarks: Partly damaged. Refers to Ārāya Tōḍara- malla Vīraṇa-nāyaka, son of Sōmaṇa-nāyaka, and Basavamba of Sāḷuguṇte, as belonging to the family of Pratāparudra and as ruling over Jagaṇāṭiguttiya-durga. States that the dam was reconstructed for the merit of his father Sōmaṇa-Nāyaka and his elder brother Basavaṇa and that the rights of enjoyment of the canal and land (kāḷuveya-bhōga and bayala-bhōga) were entrusted with the mahā- janas of the village, through Basavarasa mentioned as the dakshiṇabhujadaṇḍa of the chief.

cells.location: BŌDAN
cells.place: Slab kept in front of the Mallikārjuna temple.
cells.date: Regnal year 5, Dundubhi, Puṣhya śu 6, Friday=1142 A.D., December 25.
cells.remarks: Refers to the installation of gods Mallikārjuna and Kēśavadēva on both sides of Mūlasthānadēva by Nāranayya-daṇḍādhīśa, the prabhu of Piriya-Bōdana which was situated in Narvaṇi-12, a kampaṇa of Goṅka-120 which was a subdivision of Alande-1,000. The last mentioned division is stated as a jivita of Sānteya-Nāyaka, the taḷāra of Sarasvatipura, a town which was founded by Maḷayavatīdevī and was being administered by her mahāpradhāna-mādhava-sēnabōva, sēṇapāti, pasāvita, haḍapavaḷa and mānevarggaḍe. It records the grant of 15 kāḷadiya-mattar, 1/2 mattar of garden, a nivēśana (houses ite), measuring 20 kai, paddy-fields and money to the above mentioned gods for worship and offerings. The grant was made free of ammana and sese taxes with the consent of the officials (names mentioned). The composer of the records, Mādhava-vibhu is endowed with the epithets avadhāna-nidhāna, sahajakavi-sārvabhauma etc.

cells.date: Chālukya Vikrama year 33, Sarvadhāri, Jyēṣṭha Amāvāsya, Thursday, Solar eclipse=1108 A.D., June 11.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of 50 mattar of land to god Keśavadēva at Duttiragave, the Sarvanamaś-vada-agrahāra by Āchaladēvi, the piriyarasi of Rudra bhaṭṭōpādhyāya-sōmayāji, a person who was held in great veneration by the emperor. Out of the gift-land, which was stated to have been given by her ayyagalu (father) Ravināga-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya-sōmayāji, 30 mattar was distributed for providing for the worship and offerings to one god, 10 mattar for the priest and 10 mattar for the person who supplied flowergarlands (for the temple). It also registers a grant of a flower garden.

cells.place: Second side. No. 2. †
cells.dynasty: Krōdhi, Jyēṣṭha, Amāvāse, Monday. Probably = 1244 A.D., June 6.
cells.date: States that a certain Sarvēśvaradēvaru, led by the village-head, purchased from Koṇḍajīya, after paying gold, 30 kāla mattar of land, situated to the south of the road leading to Vēḷasaṅgavi and granted half of it (i.e., 15 mattar) for the purpose of reconstruction of the embankment after the removal of earth (accumulated in the area). A certain maṇḍalika Āhavamalla is stated to have granted the Bhōgēśvara-sthāna along with those of Dhārēśvara, Dēvaṇēśvara and Nakarēśvara to Druvēśa-bratīśvara and this grant was approved by Būṣaṇēśvara-sthāna of Vēḷugrāma. Do. (Ibid.).

cells.location: BHATKAL
cells.place: Slab lying in the compound of the Chandra-nātha basti.
cells.king: Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Chenna Bhairādēvi ruling from Sangitapura
cells.remarks: Contains Sanskrit verses composed by Vardhamāni-muni describing the families of the chief and his subordinate Nāra-nāyaka and the latter's contribution to the Jaina religion by causing the construction of a Jaina-dhāma for Vardhamāna-jinēndra. The Kannada portion renders a version of the copper-plate grant in detail pertaining to the grant of land (bidu-dēvasva) providing for the worship, offerings, āhāra-dāna, hāla dhāre etc. to Vardhamāna-tīrthaṅkara of the basti at Bhaṭakaḷa by Nāra-nāyaka, son of Vīra-nāyaka. The ruling queen is also referred to as the daughter of Mahamaṇḍalēśvara Bhairādēvi and as the daughter-in-law (snuṣā) of Sāḷuva Kṛishṇadēva-nṛipati. Published in Karnatak Inscriptions, Vol. III, Part I, No. 17.

States that certain Pāyaṇārya, the chief disciple of Vidyānandasvāmī, caused the construction of the Chaityālaya, for which the foundation-stone (Kesarv-gallu) was laid by the governor (Śaṅkara-kṣitipāla), and the installation of Pārśvatīrthēśvara was to be made subsequently and granted lands (details given) for the worship and offerings to the deity. Also refers to many other grants including the land for dānaśāle to the basadi by Saṅghirāya-arasa of Nagire, the ēḷu-maṇḍi-janaṅgoḷu, ippattuṅa lukubaḷi of Kāyikiṇi and others. Ibid., Vol. I, No. 41.

cells.location: VEṄKAṬAPURA
cells.place: Slab kept in the Venkaṭaramaṇa temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1583, Sārvari, Āśvija śu. 15, Monday, Lunar eclipse. = 1660 A.D., October 8.
cells.remarks: Refers to the chief as the son of Siddapa-nāyaka, grandson of Saṁkana-nāyaka and great grandson of Sadāśiva-nāyaka and records the grant of land situated to the west of Kukkanira-grāma in the Bhaṭṭakala-sime for the expenditure of worship, perpetual lamp, offerings and feedings at the satra of the temple of Veṅkaṭēśvara, the deity being installed earlier by one Gaṇapati-maḷḷe in the village Doṇiḍere located in Bhaṭṭakala-sime. The details of the boundaries of land and services including the gift of money for various activities in the temple are given. It also seems to state that the salary of the ambiga of the temple was to be paid out of the tax income from the satra of the temple.

cells.location: RATANPUR
cells.place: Two stone slabs built into the right side wall of the Karṇārjuni temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. Contains a detailed description of the rule of the area around Ratnapuri first under the kings of the family of Sahasārjuna till Vikrama year 1800, then for a few years under the Śūdras as feudatories of the Satārā kings, later under the Guruṇḍas and finally under the English in 1816. The temple said to have been constructed by Karṇadēva was renovated by a Vaiśya Mahara whose genealogy is also given. The praśasti was composed by Rēvārāma whose genealogy is also given in detail. It was probably engraved by the goldsmith (svarṇakārin) Rāmaprasāda, the son of Jayakṛishṇa and the grandson of Darīyābasimha. It was probably written by Sītārāma. (Noticed in Hiralal's Inscriptions in the C.P. and Berar (Second edition), p. 130, No. 215).

cells.location: BALSŪR
cells.place: Slab kept in front of Nīlakaṇṭheśvara temple.
cells.date: Regnal year 7, Piṁgala, Mārggaśira ba. Amāvāse, Monday, Solar eclipse. Irregular.
cells.remarks: Do. Records the grant of 500 mattar of land to god Svayambhu Nīlakaṇṭhadēva and[500] mattar of land to the twenty-five (Ippattay-varu) brāhmaṇas of Sīvūru by Māṇṇeya Pithuvarasa, Bapparasa of Moraṁba the Prabhugaḷu mīligaru of Sīvūru and Masaṇeya Sāhaṇi with the acceptance of mahāpradhāna Devaṇa-nāyaka and [Jaggaya]-nāyaka. The grant was made for the worship, offerings etc. to the above god and for the benefit of the twenty-five brāhmaṇas of Śivapura of Sīrūru who are praised in eloquent terms.

cells.location: KAUTHA
cells.place: Slab kept in front of the Viṣṇu temple.
cells.date: Regnal year 26, Vṛisha, Solar eclipse =1101 A.D., April 30, Tuesday.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Contains a number of verses and gives the genealogy of the king and his subordinate perggaḍe Māchirāja (whose family details are given) of Vipra-kula. The latter is stated to have constructed a temple to the deity Svayambhu Kalidēvasvāmi at Kavithage and granted 160 mattar of land and 2 mattar of garden as taḷavṛitti and also the tax-income accruing from biḷkoḍe, hejjunka, vaḍḍarāvuḷa, maṇḍara, āvaṭa, nelameḷḷu and kigu-kuḷa of the Kavithage village. The grant was made as paramēśvara-datti for making permanent provisions for worship, offerings, maintenance of a satra, free education (bahu-śāstra-dāna) etc. along with a copper plate charter. States that the record was composed by saikavi Kāḷidāsa.

cells.location: KALLUMADAI †
cells.place: West base.
cells.remarks: Records the sale (kāraṇmai-kaṇi-vilaippramāṇam) of hereditary tenancy rights of lands by the ūrār of Pūmbiljal Muṭṭaraiyankōṭṭai in Paruṭṭikkudi-nāḍu and of Kaṇmiyārkōṭṭai to Tēvāram-Aḷagiyav Muḍaliyar, one of the kaikōḷas, for the land value of 300 varāhan-paṇam. The ūrār seem to have endowed the income from taxes on these lands to the deity Tiruppālaiyūr-uḍaiya-nāyaṇār. It seems to record that any settlements could be made in this kāraṇmai-kaṇi and it was decided by the ūrār not to collect the taxes (names specified) from the settlements thus made and to accept them as ūr-kuḍi. Do.

cells.location: TARUVAI
cells.place: Śiva temple, north wall.
cells.remarks: Begins with the praśasti Puṉalar tiru, etc., and states that the king while seated on the throne named paḷḷippaḍai (paḷḷippaḍam) Maḷavarāyaṉ in his palace at Madurai in the subdivision Māḍakkulakkiḻ in Madurōdaya-vaḷanāḍu issued this order to the Śivabrāhmaṇas and tāṉapati of the temple of Pāṇḍīśvaram-uḍaiyār to the effect that the lands in the village Taruvai, a western hamlet of Śrīvallabha-maṅgalam in Kiṭalakak-kūṟṟam should be provided for the food offerings of the deity. The boundaries of the gift lands are mentioned. In characters of the 13th century.

cells.location: DŪDHPĀNĪ
cells.place: A stone slab.
cells.remarks: States that, at a time when the villages of Bhramaraśālmalī, Chhiṅgala and Bhūtiṣandaka were without rulers, Ādi siṃha, the lord of Magadha, went there for hunting elephants. On his asking for an escort, the villagers requested Udayamāna, a merchant-emigrant, to do the job. On his successful completion of the assignment, the villagers made him the ruler of Bhramaraśālmalī. He, in his turn, proclaimed his brothers Śrīdhautamāna and Ajitamāna respectively as the rulers of Chhiṅgala and Bhūtiṣandaka. In characters of about the 9th century A.D. Contra. Ep. Ind., Vol. II. pp. 344 ff.; Bhandarkar's list, No, 1743.

cells.location: BĀRI
cells.place: In the eastern wall of a step-well in the village.
cells.date: Regnal year 30, A.H. 1097 (words & chronogram) = 1686 A.D., July-November
cells.remarks: Damaged. States that Bahādur Shāh son of ‘Ālam Shāh and grandson of Fīrūz Shāh constructed ‘this well’ in a grden in the path of God (i.e. for public use). Also states that Bahādur Shāh had succeeded his father and grand-father, who was one of the sons of Qādir Shāh, a brother of Tughluq Shāh and had established his rule at Kaipī. ‘Ālam Shāh held authority at Chanderi, while the builder Bahādur Shāh, at Bāri. Cf. Gwalior Rājya-ke-Abhilekh, p. 87, No. 41. For an inscription of almost identical purport from Malhārgaṛh, same district, see A.R.Ep., 1967-68 No. 244 of Appendix D.

cells.place: Concld. KAIMGANJ TAHSIL—Contd. FARRUKHABAD DISTRICT—Contd. UTTAR PRADESH—Contd.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a Rest-House (Bishrānt, i.e. Vishrānt) on the bank of the sacred river Ganges for the benefit of the people who came for the holy dip, by Rāi Nahl Dās son of Lālā Khub Chand, the Superintendent (Nāzim). The builder was born at the town (qaṣba) Klor Glodnahr and was a high revenue official under Amīnu’d-Daula, the Deputy or Chief Minister (Nā’ib) in the time of (Nawwāb) Nāṣir Jang Bangash, the Viceroy (Nā’ib) of the Mughal emperor. The epigraph also states that by this time the British had established their hold on India. It further states that the Rāi Ṣāḥib, in compliance with the order of Gaṅgājī (the Ganges) to provide a suitable table to people, great and small, coming for a dip before worship, constructed it under the supervision of Barguzar Parṣhād.

cells.remarks: States that this Sarāi and pucca Bridge built 50 years ago by Nawwāb Muntazimud-Daula Bahādur Ḥakīm Mahdī Alī K̲h̲ān, have been handed over, along with the land and shops in front of the Sarāi, by Nawwāb Mīrzā'ī Begam Ṣāḥiba, the heiress of the Nawwāb to the Municipality of the city of Shāhjahānpūr for meeting the expenses (of their maintenance).
